title: The Armchair Technologist. Part 2b: the Resurgent Technologist
html:
The Armchair Technologist. Part 2b: the Resurgent Technologist

In my initial post in the Armchair Technologist series, I questioned if a former technician could become a Armchair Technologist after a significant period of time not using their technical skills. I raised the question partly as a self reflection. While I have started using the title Resurgent Technologist, I want to give kudos to Craig Williams who referred to such individuals, in comment on an earlier post the series, as a Rusty Expert. And, I found his definition quite clear and easy to understand as he noted that “they retain enough knowledge to envisage a technology in-context and perhaps have the influence to make it happen”.

In today’s fast-paced technological landscape, it’s easy to overlook the potential of individuals who have transitioned from technical roles to managerial positions. These “resurgent technologists” (or rusty experts) possess a unique blend of technical expertise and leadership skills that can be a significant asset to any organization.

While their day-to-day responsibilities may have shifted away from coding or system administration, their foundational understanding of technology remains. This knowledge allows them to:

  • Identify Opportunities: Spot potential areas for technological innovation and improvement.
  • Assess Risks: Evaluate the potential risks and benefits of new technologies.
  • Make Informed Decisions: Base decisions on a solid understanding of technical feasibility and business impact.

Beyond their technical acumen, resurgent technologists can also play crucial roles in:

  • Mentoring and Guiding: Sharing their experience and knowledge with younger, less experienced team members.
  • Leading Innovative Teams: Inspiring and motivating teams to think creatively and embrace new technologies.
  • Defining Realistic Projects: Setting achievable goals and breaking down complex projects into manageable tasks.
  • Enhancing Collaboration: Fostering effective communication and collaboration between technical and non-technical teams.
  • Governance and Risk Management: Ensuring compliance with regulations and standards while mitigating security risks.

To fully leverage the potential of resurgent technologists, organizations should prioritize their continuous learning and development. This can be achieved through:

  • Training Programs: Providing opportunities to learn about emerging technologies and industry best practices.
  • Mentorship: Pairing resurgent technologists with experienced mentors to share knowledge and insights.
  • Exposure to Innovation: Encouraging participation in innovation initiatives and hackathons.

By investing in the development of resurgent technologists, organizations can unlock a wealth of innovation, improve efficiency, and achieve long-term success. These individuals can serve as strategic assets, driving digital transformation and ensuring the organization’s competitiveness in the ever-evolving technological landscape.

Andrej
teaser: Why a former technician years away from hands-on work can still be a strategic asset: the Resurgent Technologist, or Rusty Expert.
